title: Do You Need Lovable If You Already Pay for Claude? (October 2026)

body_markdown:
For most people who already pay for Claude, no. Claude does the thinking, and most of what Lovable adds is hosting: a backend, a database, logins, and a live URL. If you want to build inside Claude, you need a place to run the app, not a second AI. If you want a separate visual editor, Lovable fits.


## The short version:


Claude Pro is $20 a month and includes artifacts and Claude Code.


Lovable Pro is $25 a month and runs on its own credit balance, which pays for building, hosting, and in-app AI from one pool.


Claude can write almost any app, but on its own it does not host a backend, a database, or logins for your users.


On Floot, you build inside Claude and Floot hosts the full stack, so there is no second AI bill.


On a second builder, you pay two companies to think about one app. The rest of this guide covers what a second tool actually adds, how to decide, what each path makes you do, and the billing detail that can take a live app down.


## Claude and Lovable, in one picture


Think of building a house. Claude is the architect: it draws the plans and redraws them when you change your mind.


What you do not have yet is the building: land, walls, and an address people can visit. Adding Lovable is hiring a second architect who happens to own a lot. You get the land, but you pay two people to draw one house.


The split matters because thinking and running are different jobs: thinking happens once per change, and running happens every minute your users are there.


## What a second tool actually adds


A builder like Lovable earns its keep on four jobs, and none of them is the AI.


It stores data. A signup or a booking goes into a database (the filing cabinet the app reads and writes).


It checks who people are. Logins with Google or email, and rules about who sees what.


It hosts the app on a live address. A real URL you can send to a customer, on a computer that is always on.


It updates the live app. Add feature #12 and the running app changes without you touching a server.


Notice the pattern. Every one of those is about running the app, and Claude already writes it.


## Build inside Claude, or in a separate editor?


Ask where you want to be when you type "add a page for invoices."


If the answer is inside Claude, a second builder is a second tab and a second bill. You need hosting that plugs into Claude.


If the answer is a separate editor where you click a button and change it directly, Lovable fits. It has a visual edit mode and two-way GitHub sync, and it makes sense as your only tool if you do not pay for Claude.


If the app needs no logins or saved data, like a pricing calculator, you can skip both and use Claude alone. If customers sign in and upload files, like a client portal, you need hosting.


## What each tool makes you do


Every path gets you an app. The difference is how many AI bills you pay and who runs it once it is live.


Claude alone gives you artifacts, which are pages Claude makes inside the chat, on every plan including Free (per claude.com/pricing, Sept 25, 2026). They suit a one-screen tool, not a product with accounts. Claude Code (Pro $20 a month, Max from $100) writes a full-stack app on your computer, then you set up the host, database, and logins yourself. Lovable charges a plan (Pro $25 a month, Business $50, as of Sept 25, 2026) plus one credit balance that its docs say lets you "build apps, chat with Lovable, run deployed apps, and power AI features." Edits cost 0.50 to 1.70 credits each, Pro adds 5 daily credits to a monthly grant.


The pattern is the same everywhere it goes wrong: you pay for AI twice just to get the app hosted.


Floot adds the part Claude is missing, inside Claude, so you do not need a second builder. You describe the app in the chat you already use, and your assistant builds it onto Floot: pages for what people see, small server programs called endpoints for what the app does ("book a slot," "send the invoice"), and a Postgres database for what it remembers. Floot hosts all of it on a live URL from the first build. Because Floot also includes the database, logins with Google, Microsoft, and email, file storage, email sending, scheduled jobs, and live updates, everything Lovable adds on top of Claude is already there. You never sign up for anything else, and the thinking stays on your Claude plan, so there is no second AI bill. Floot meters its own work in building actions, which reset daily: Free 100 a day, Pro $25 a month for 1,000, Power $100 a month for 5,000.


## FAQ


## Do I need Lovable if I have Claude?


Usually not. The missing piece is hosting, a database, and logins, which a connector like Floot adds without a second AI bill.


## Can Claude replace Lovable?


Claude replaces the AI part, not the hosting.


## Is Lovable worth it if I pay for Claude?


Yes, if you want its visual editor. If you mainly want a Claude-built app hosted, you are paying for AI twice.


## Lovable vs Claude: which is better for building apps?


They do different jobs. Claude is a general AI you build with, and Lovable is a builder that also hosts the app.


## Does Lovable use one credit balance for everything?


Yes. Since August 2026, one balance covers building, hosting on Lovable Cloud, and in-app AI.


## Does Floot work inside Claude?


Yes. Add Floot's connector to Claude, describe the app, and Floot builds and hosts it with the database and logins included.
